grade.basis: Whole single-movement sonata-form quartet: inspected all eight pages of the complete score (mm.1–122), including the opening, the sustained running passage at mm.36–43, lyrical middle section at mm.46–76, recapitulation, and mm.106–122 coda. Violin 1 carries the high ledger-line melody, chromatic turns, repeated slurred sixteenth-note scales, shifts and accented double stops; violins 2–4 chiefly have slower accompaniment and double-stopped pulses. These recurring demands fit level 4 (ABRSM 7/RCM 8), near the Bach Double/Dvořák Sonatina anchors, rather than diploma technique. The ensemble has matched releases, dynamics and some conversational entries, but the accompaniment is regular enough that no extra coordination level is justified.

grade.basis: Whole two-movement work: inspected every page of the eight-page complete score. The Adagio (pp.1–3) is largely manageable lyrical writing, but the Allegretto in 3/8 (dotted quarter=68, pp.3–8) requires violin 1 to shift into a substantially higher ledger-line register, deliver rapid chromatic sixteenth-note and tuplet flourishes, and execute the explicitly marked saltellato passage (around m.51). Its final poco più mosso coda sustains a very high repeated-note figure before chordal closing gestures. Violin 2 shares occasional runs but is generally less demanding. The repeated upper-register, chromatic and bow-control demands place the whole first part around level 5 (ABRSM 8/RCM 9), comparable in technical category to the local La Folia/advanced Baroque anchors, with a plausible one-level downward uncertainty. Frequent pizzicato/arco exchanges and pickups require rehearsal, but do not independently raise the grade.

grade.basis: Whole four-movement work: inspected all notation in the nine-page imposed Merton score PDF, which contains printed score pages 3–15 (Allegro espressivo, Scherzo/Trio, Larghetto and Finale). Violin 1 repeatedly occupies the above-staff ledger-line register and needs secure shifts and clean articulated leaps in the Allegro assai Scherzo and Finale; the Larghetto has flowing chromatic sixteenth-note passages and sustained expressive shaping. Lower parts are predominantly single-line, with regular pulse, staggered entries, occasional faster figures and dynamic transitions. The whole-work demands fit level 4 (ABRSM 7/RCM 8), around the local Bach Double and Haydn Op.33 No.2 anchors; neither extended virtuoso passagework nor specialist advanced technique is a persistent requirement. Four-part intonation and ensemble timing matter, but the rhythmic vocabulary is sufficiently regular that no automatic quartet uplift is applied.
